steps.say: Ptosis is grading against the inframammary fold. Grade one is parking the nipple at the fold, grade two is dropping it below the fold but above the lowest contour, and grade three is sinking it to the lowest point. Pseudoptosis is keeping the nipple up while gland is bottoming out below.
steps.tx: **Regnault** classification (the breast ptosis grading against the fold) defines **Grade I** nipple at the **inframammary fold** **IMF** (the crease under the breast), **Grade II** nipple below IMF but above lower breast contour, **Grade III** nipple at the lowest contour point, and **pseudoptosis** (false droop) with the nipple at or above IMF plus glandular bottoming out. Grade decides pedicle and skin pattern.

The image shows four side views of the breast with nipple position judged against a horizontal fold reference line. This teaches **Regnault** grading, from **Grade I** at the fold through deeper grades to **pseudoptosis** where the nipple stays up while gland sags. Accurate grade guides choice of pedicle and skin pattern.
steps.say: The picture shows four profiles moving from nipple at the crease to nipple at the lowest contour, plus a form where only gland drops. It shows how to grade droop by nipple height relative to the fold. The grade matters because it decides which blood supply and which scar pattern will be safe.

vis.alt: Four breast profiles showing nipple height relative to fold reference line shown.
vis.caption: Graded breast droop from mild to false droop Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Huge breasts are needing the broadest blood supply. The inferior pedicle Wise pattern inverted-T is remaining the workhorse for massive macromastia. A wide inferior dermoglandular pedicle is carrying the nipple-areola complex safely, and sensation is being preserved.
steps.tx: **Inferior pedicle** **Wise pattern** (anchor-scar reduction on a lower-pole carrier) inverted-T reduction mammaplasty is the workhorse for massive **macromastia** (symptomatic breast hypertrophy), reliably preserving nipple-areola complex **NAC** (nipple plus areola) sensation and vascularity. Length and safety are its strengths; maximal projection is not.

**Superomedial pedicle** (upper-inner carrier) technique supplies the **NAC** via internal thoracic anterior **perforators** (chest-wall vessels) and superior vessels, providing excellent **upper pole projection** (upper-breast fullness) and fullness. It suits moderate reductions where shape outranks maximal resection weight, unlike the inferior workhorse.
steps.say: Upper fullness is coming from a superomedial blood supply. Internal thoracic anterior perforators with superior vessels are feeding the nipple-areola complex. Excellent upper pole projection is suiting moderate reductions where shape is outranking weight.

The horizontal scar is disappearing in the vertical technique. The Lejour vertical scar reduction is dropping the transverse inframammary limb entirely. Parenchymal remodelling with pillar sutures plus stretchy skin retraction is doing the shaping.
steps.tx: **Vertical scar** reduction mammaplasty (**Lejour** technique, lollipop-scar shaping) eliminates the transverse **inframammary scar** (the anchor's horizontal limb), relying on extensive parenchymal remodelling and **skin elasticity** (shrink-wrap retraction). Less scarring trades against a learning curve with temporary gathering that settles. Temporary gathering around the areola settles within weeks.

steps.say: Extreme length is defeating pedicles. Once the suprasternal notch to nipple distance is passing thirty five to forty centimetres, perfusion is failing. A free nipple graft is eliminating torsion and necrosis risk by replacing the complex as a graft.
steps.tx: **Free nipple graft** **FNG** (nipple-areola lifted and replaced as a full-thickness graft) is indicated in **gigantomastia** (extreme hypertrophy) with suprasternal notch to nipple distance exceeding **35** to **40 cm**, eliminating any risk of pedicle torsion and necrosis. Sensation is sacrificed for safety at these lengths.

rows: No pedicle torsion or necrosis risk

steps.say: Nipple feeling is travelling with the fourth intercostal nerve. Its lateral cutaneous branch is piercing deep fascia at the mid-axillary line and is running forward to the nipple. Wide lateral undermining is endangering it, so sensation-sparing plans are respecting this path.
steps.tx: Nipple sensation is primarily mediated by the lateral cutaneous branch of the **fourth intercostal nerve**, piercing deep fascia at the **mid-axillary line** (the vertical side-chest line). Lateral resections that cross this course deaden the nipple, while medial-based pedicles leave it untouched.

The image shows a side view of the breast with the T4 nerve travelling forward to the nipple after piercing fascia at the mid axillary line, with a lateral danger zone marked. Sensation depends on the **fourth intercostal nerve** via its lateral cutaneous branch. Wide **lateral dissection** threatens it, while **medial** based work leaves the path untouched.
steps.say: The picture shows the nerve route from the side chest wall forward into the nipple, with the outer zone flagged as risky. It teaches that feeling in the nipple travels mainly with the fourth chest nerve. Cutting widely on the outer side can deaden feeling, so plans that stay medial protect sensation.

vis.alt: Side breast section showing T4 nerve path to nipple with outer danger zone shown.
vis.caption: Nerve course to nipple with outer dissection risk zone Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Blood supply NAC** (nipple-areola complex perfusion) is multi-source, derived from **anterior intercostal perforators** of the **internal mammary** artery (breastbone-side chest vessels), the **lateral thoracic** artery (armpit-side supply), and **thoracoacromial** branches (upper-pole contributors). No single named vessel owns the complex, which is why most pedicle orientations survive.
steps.say: Many vessels are sharing the nipple-areola supply. Anterior intercostal perforators from the internal mammary, lateral thoracic branches, and thoracoacromial twigs are all contributing. No single artery is owning the complex, so most pedicle designs are staying safe.

Mild droop is tightening through the areolar border alone. The Benelli round-block periareolar mastopexy is cinching a purse-string permanent suture around the areola. Grade one ptosis is correcting with barely visible scarring, though projection gain is staying modest.
steps.tx: **Benelli** round-block **periareolar mastopexy** (doughnut lift around the areola) utilizes a **purse-string** permanent suture (a cinching loop gathering skin) to correct mild **Grade I** ptosis with minimal visible scarring. The ring hides at the areolar edge; projection gain stays modest and temporary pleating is accepted.
